item.content:encoded:
The horror of this doesn't do anything for me. Having a character scream in eternal pain has been an overused trope of horror/sci-fi for as long as I can remember, and having that character be an A.I. doesn't do anything to elevate it above that status. That being said, I thoroughly enjoyed the quality of the writing here and its ability to work without any prior understanding of the canon.

This is a +1 from me.

item.content:encoded: Simple, elegant, horrific. Perfect example of what SCP literature can be when done well.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Ok, so this is good.

The pacing and build-up are masterfully executed (considering the tale's very short size), and your word choice is nicely put all around. Each segment dwelves more and more on this man's emotions and its plot in a way that does not seems rushed or forced.

It has a nice progression to it, and the final stanzas are the cherry on top. Like said above, previous understanding of the lore behind it isn't necessary to full enjoyment of the article, and it's a pretty damn good stand-alone (as I myself never read anything from its canon).

Wrapping this up, this is great, and you should be proud of yourself. Really interested in your next, similar works, as poetry is far from being explored on the wiki.

+1

item.title: Author Post
item.content:encoded:
Spooky, right?

I wrote this as a non-SCP thing when I got the idea, then realised how heavily SCP-related it was, then put together this version in an afternoon. It's the shortest thing I've ever written, and I probably spent as much time on the formatting as I did on the text — it was one of those real "bolt from the blue" type concepts. I lukewarm-posted, with essentially no changes after getting critique, but my heart goes out to the two or three people who looked it over beforehand and gave me the confidence to post.

I'm super glad to see you all like this sort of thing as much as I do :)
